MVBeliefUpdatr: Fitting, Summarizing, and Visualizing of Gaussian Ideal Observers and Adaptors

Source: R/MVBeliefUpdatr-package.R
MVBeliefUpdatr-package.Rd

Model, fit, and visualize incremental Bayesian categorization and belief updating for uni- and multivariate Gaussian, cue integration, and exemplar-based cognitive models using 'S7' class architecture. Provides tools for simulating normative ideal observers and ideal adaptors under conjugate priors including Normal-Inverse-Chi-squared (NIX), Multivariate Normal-Inverse-Chi-squared (MNIX), and Normal-Inverse-Wishart (NIW) distributions. Supports Bayesian parameter inference via Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling using 'Stan', model comparison via 'loo', and rich visualizations with 'ggplot2' and 'patchwork'.

Overview

MVBeliefUpdatr provides a unified, object-oriented framework for Bayesian ideal observers, ideal adaptors, incremental belief updating, and hierarchical Bayesian cognitive modeling.

The package supports continuous distributional representations (univariate Gaussian, multivariate Gaussian, multi-univariate Gaussian cue integration), conjugate prior distributions over category parameters (Normal-Inverse- Chisquare, Normal-Inverse-Wishart), and exemplar-based representations.

Using analytical conjugate updating or hierarchical Bayesian inference in Stan via rstan, MVBeliefUpdatr facilitates simulation, parameter estimation, categorization prediction, and visualization of speech perception and perceptual adaptation experiments.

S7 Core Class Architecture

All model objects are organized under an explicit, compositional S7 class hierarchy:

MVBU_CategoryRepresentation

Abstract base class for individual category representations, encapsulating category parameters, cue labels, and likelihood functions.

MVBU_CategoryRepresentationTemplate

Validated collection of category representations forming a perceptual inventory or template.

MVBU_CognitiveModel

Decision model pairing a category template with decision behavior (decision rule, category priors, lapse rate, lapse bias, and perceptual noise).

MVBU_IdealObserver

Subclass of MVBU_CognitiveModel for observers with fixed generative category distributions.

MVBU_IdealAdaptor

Subclass of MVBU_CognitiveModel for adaptors with conjugate prior beliefs that update incrementally from exposure.

MVBU_Stanfit

Wrapper for rstan stanfit objects inferring prior beliefs, lapse parameters, and noise from behavioral test data.

MVBU_StanfitInput

Container for exposure data, test data, priors, and transformation functions used to prepare Stan inputs.

MVBU_Staninput

Validated input data list passed to Stan models.

Supported Model Families

MVBeliefUpdatr provides concrete S7 classes and constructors across seven families:

UVG / NIX

Univariate Gaussian ideal observers (UVG_IdealObserver) and Normal-Inverse-Chisquare ideal adaptors (NIX_IdealAdaptor).

MUVG / MNIX

Multi-univariate Gaussian ideal observers (MUVG_IdealObserver) and independent Normal-Inverse-Chisquare cue integration adaptors (MNIX_IdealAdaptor).

MVG / NIW

Multivariate Gaussian ideal observers (MVG_IdealObserver) and Normal-Inverse-Wishart ideal adaptors (NIW_IdealAdaptor).

EXEMPLAR

Exemplar-based categorization models (Exemplar_Model) with kernel density estimation over stored exemplars.

Acknowledgments

Belief-updating formulations build upon conjugate Bayesian theory (Murphy 2012) , phonetic sliding template models (Nearey and Assmann 2007) , Dave Kleinschmidt's BeliefUpdatr (Kleinschmidt and Jaeger 2011) , (Kleinschmidt and Jaeger 2012) , (Kleinschmidt and Jaeger 2015) , (Kleinschmidt and Jaeger 2016) , and unsupervised adaptation modeling (Yan and Jaeger 2018) .

Contributions and feedback from Zach Burchill, Anna Persson, and Xin Xie are gratefully acknowledged.

Kleinschmidt DF, Jaeger TF (2012). “A continuum of phonetic adaptation : Evaluating an incremental belief-updating model of recalibration and selective adaptation.” In Proceedings of the 34th Annual Meeting of the Cognitive Science Society (CogSci12), 605-610.

Kleinschmidt DF, Jaeger TF (2015). “Robust speech perception: Recognize the familiar, generalize to the similar, and adapt to the novel.” Psychological Review, 122(2), 148-203. ISSN 0033-295X. doi:10.1037/a0038695 . http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/25844873.

Kleinschmidt DF, Jaeger TF (2016). “What do you expect from an unfamiliar talker?” In Trueswell JC, Papafragou A, Grodner D, Mirman D (eds.), Proceedings of the 38th Annual Meeting of the Cognitive Science Society.

Murphy KP (2012). Machine learning: a probabilistic perspective. MIT Press.

Nearey TM, Assmann PF (2007). “Probabilistic 'sliding template' models for indirect vowel normalization.” In Solé M, Beddor PS, Ohala M (eds.), Experimental Approaches to Phonology, 246–269. Oxford University Press, Oxford.
